A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CODI and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F. Content can be matched across the substantial reorganization, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CODI mathematical-reasoning results, ablations, efficiency measurements, and interpretability analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original mathematical-reasoning experiments and adds CommonsenseQA results and expanded baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The shared teacher/student model, three losses, colon-token distillation, continuous-state propagation, and inference procedure remain unchanged. LayerNorm added to the example code in Figure A3 implements a component already described in v1, rather than establishing a new method.

E1.justification: v2 adds training on CommonsenseQA-CoT and evaluation on CommonsenseQA, extending the work from arithmetic to multiple-choice commonsense reasoning. The mathematical datasets and decoded-pattern training tasks are retained.

E2.justification: v1 Table 1 includes Coconut only for GPT-2 on GSM8k. v2 Figure 3 and Table 1 add Coconut to the retained GSM8k-NL, LLaMA GSM8k, and three OOD comparisons, substantially completing comparisons against the principal competing method. Figure 4 also includes Coconut and iCoT in the efficiency comparison.

E3.justification: The added CommonsenseQA experiment trains on correctness-filtered GPT-4o-mini rationales and evaluates on 1,221 validation questions. Appendix A explicitly states that iCoT/Coconut training does not use LoRA, qualifying v1's general LoRA description, and provides additional Coconut schedules. These reported settings do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 removes the jointly trained independent-teacher ablation from v1 Table 3 and the training-accuracy analysis from v1 Appendix D. Most ablations, thought-count sensitivity, and interpretability analyses remain. The Res/Op-Res experiment moves from Section 5.2 to Appendix D rather than being removed.

E5.justification: Both versions average ten CoT-SFT samples at temperature 0.1 and report one run for the deterministic methods. Neither introduces confidence intervals, significance tests, training-seed variation, or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 3 adds CommonsenseQA results: CODI versus CoT-SFT scores 44.0% versus 36.9% on GPT-2 and 74.0% versus 68.2% on LLaMA; No-CoT-SFT reaches 74.9% on LLaMA. Coconut gains previously missing mathematical result entries, while retained mathematical accuracies stay unchanged. The 42.7% joint-teacher result and training-accuracy entries disappear. The verbose-CoT summary changes from 62.1 tokens/7.8× compression to 65.5/8.2× alongside a consolidated display, without establishing faster inference.

T1.justification: The CoT-shift statement and Appendix B derivation, including the softmax/scaling simplification, are unchanged. Reordered equations and clarified teacher-target notation introduce no new formal result or proof correction.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly limits the abstract's GSM8k parity claim to GPT-2 scale, removes scalability from the primary contribution list, and qualifies interpretability as a reasonable level rather than transparent reasoning. The central self-distillation and compression claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 drops the warm-up/shared-representation justification for self-distillation and emphasizes reference learning and training efficiency. It adds hypotheses about commonsense results and teacher-pattern mismatch. Section 7 adds multi-token probing and large-model resource limitations while removing the deterministic-reasoning and mathematics-only caveats, substantially revising the discussion of mechanisms and applicability.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the LLaMA Instruct checkpoint, baseline LoRA exclusions, Coconut learning rates and schedules, and CommonsenseQA construction and statistics. Figure A3 gains the previously documented LayerNorm. The new Coconut paragraph labels its LLaMA schedule 'iCoT', leaving that attribution ambiguous.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the neuroscience-based motivation with prompt-learning and computational-efficiency positioning. It adds substantive comparisons with concurrent latent-reasoning and looped-transformer work, including SoftCoT, Token Assorted, and recurrent-depth approaches, distinguishing CODI's fine-tuning and additional-token strategy. These works are discussed rather than newly benchmarked.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. Teacher and student subsections are reordered, self-distillation receives a separate subsection, OOD evaluation becomes a dedicated section, and pattern learning moves to the appendix. Limitations and several experimental explanations are substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn. The main results table becomes bar charts plus a separate OOD table, and the efficiency table becomes a dual-axis plot. Case-study graphics are reformatted and omit the universally attended first token. Tables and appendix examples are reorganized, while the thought-count plot is retained.

improvement.justification: The CommonsenseQA experiments provide evidence beyond arithmetic, and expanded Coconut comparisons close important comparator gaps. More qualified parity and interpretability claims improve calibration. These gains are moderated by removal of supporting training-accuracy and joint-teacher analyses, omission of the deterministic-reasoning limitation, and less precise efficiency reporting, yielding a limited net improvement.
